findings.summary: WikiStore._load_index unconditionally erases the recorded degradation reason at startup, defeating INV-4's explicit requirement that index_health.last_error '保留原始异常文本而非类名'. _search._ensure_lancedb() (search.py:158-160) and the drop/recreate block (store.py:63-65) both set _last_error and flip _mode to 'keyword_only' on failure, but store.py:68 then assigns _search._last_error = None afterwards. In the most realistic degradation path — lancedb unavailable/unimportable, or the table recreate failing — every subsequent wiki_search/wiki_query response reports {mode: 'keyword_only', last_error: null}, i.e. a silently dead vector index with no diagnosable cause. That is exactly the v1 root cause spec §9 and INV-4 exist to prevent, and no test covers index_health after a lancedb-layer failure.

The persisted keyword index accumulates ghost page ids forever. _load_index constructs a fresh KeywordIndex, loads keyword.json (which still contains ids of pages deleted or renamed in earlier sessions), and then re-adds all live pages, so stale ids are never pruned and are written back by the next _mutate save. Those ids consume slots in _rrf_fuse's top_k ranking while wiki_search silently drops them (find_page_by_id returns None), degrading recall for real pages across restarts. Loading keyword.json contributes nothing else, since every live page is re-indexed immediately after.

migrate() writes migration-report.json after the initial commit, so the freshly produced v2 data repo is left with an untracked file and a non-empty `git status --porcelain`. Spec §7 lists migration-report.json among the 产出物 of a run that is supposed to be a '全量 initial commit', and INV-5 requires the worktree to be clean between calls; a server opened on a migrated repo (the A7 hand-off path) therefore starts dirty, and no test asserts cleanliness of the migrate output.

wiki_delete is the only mutation that still derives its target path and id from the page read before the lock is taken; unlike wiki_update/wiki_edit/wiki_rename it never re-reads the page inside _write. If a concurrent rename or delete commits in between, full.unlink() raises FileNotFoundError, which is not a StoreError and so escapes the `except StoreError` handler as a raw traceback instead of the structured {code, message} error required by spec §9.

Every WikiStore construction drops the persisted lancedb table and re-embeds all pages synchronously inside __init__. This correctly removes the duplicate-row growth flagged previously, but it means each server start issues one embedding request per page against the configured production endpoint, so startup cost and index availability scale linearly with corpus size and no incremental reuse of the on-disk vector table remains.
